author: high
claim: Let D_n(x_1,...,x_n) be the determinant in the target identity. For n>=2, D_n(x_1,...,x_n)=\prod_{i=2}^n(x_i-x_1)D_{n-1}(x_2,...,x_n).
evidence: Write the columns as C_1,...,C_n. In descending order k=n,n-1,...,2 replace C_k by C_k-x_1C_{k-1}. At the moment of each replacement C_{k-1} is still an original column, so the new entry in row i, column k is x_i^{k-1}-x_1x_i^{k-2}=(x_i-x_1)x_i^{k-2}. These determinant-preserving column operations make the first row (1,0,...,0). Laplace expansion along that row leaves the submatrix indexed by rows 2,...,n and columns 2,...,n. Factoring x_i-x_1 from each remaining row i yields the stated recurrence, because the residual entries are x_i^{k-2}, the Vandermonde matrix of size n-1 on x_2,...,x_n.

links.statement: The descending column-operation recurrence for the Vandermonde determinant.

glossary.D_n(x_1,...,x_n): the determinant of the n by n matrix whose entry in row i and column k is x_i^{k-1}
glossary.C_k: the kth column of that matrix
